A second chance at HSC, but not at university admission

Students sitting next month’s HSC supplementary examinations are set to miss admission tests at 14 public universities, as application deadlines close before their results are published, despite an appeal from the University Grants Commission.

Arafat Rahaman18 November 2026 · Updated 18 November 2026
18 November 20265 min readThe Daily Star

Students sitting next month’s HSC supplementary examinations are set to miss admission tests at 14 public universities, as application deadlines close before their results are published, despite an appeal from the University Grants Commission.

The institutions include Dhaka University, Jahangirnagar University, Bangladesh University of Engineering and Technology, Khulna University of Engineering and Technology, Bangladesh Maritime University and nine agricultural universities.

Together, they offered more than 14,000 first-year seats last session, over a fifth of the roughly 63,000 seats on public university main campuses.

On November 9, the UGC urged public universities to open applications in January and hold admission tests from February to accommodate supplementary examinees.

Of the 5,94,113 candidates who failed this year’s HSC and equivalent examinations, 4,22,905 failed in up to two subjects and qualified for retakes.

The supplementary examinations, being held for the first time, will run from December 1 to 15, with results expected by December 31.

DU will close applications on November 25 and hold admission tests from December 5 to 26.

Candidates whose grades improve after HSC answer-script re-scrutiny, with results due on November 23, will get two additional days to apply. However, DU’s admission circular makes no such provision for supplementary examinees.

“We do not agree with the UGC’s decision. We have no involvement in the decision taken by the UGC,” DU Pro-Vice-Chancellor (Administration) Prof Mohammed Almujaddade Alfasane told The Daily Star.

DU officials said rescheduling could cause another session jam, noting that it took four years to clear the Covid-19 backlog.

JU will accept applications from November 22 to December 15, with admission tests tentatively scheduled for January 10-21. Its circular lists 1,848 seats but offers no provision for provisional applications from retakers.

Applications for the agricultural cluster, comprising Bangladesh Agricultural University, Sher-e-Bangla Agricultural University, Sylhet Agricultural University and six others, will run from November 25 to December 15. The admission test is scheduled for January 2.

Prof Md Abdul Latif, vice-chancellor of Sher-e-Bangla Agricultural University and cluster coordinator, disputed that retakers were excluded, saying qualified students could sit the test.

He said rescheduling would be difficult as universities generally hold admission tests on Fridays and Saturdays. However, the cluster would reconsider if instructed by the education ministry.

Buet will hold its admission test on January 16, retaining its HSC GPA-5 requirement. Kuet’s application deadline is December 10, with the test scheduled for January 8. Bangladesh Maritime University will hold tests on December 29 and 30.

The schedules particularly affect science students seeking admission to engineering and agricultural universities and medical colleges.

The medical and dental admission test is expected on December 18.

However, several universities have made arrangements to accommodate supplementary examinees.

RU will hold admission tests on February 12, 13 and 20. Although applications run from November 15 to 30, supplementary passers will get seven days after their results are published to apply.

CU will accept applications until January 10 and hold tests from January 29 to February 8. Khulna University has rescheduled its tests from December 17-18 to February 4-5.

Jagannath University will allow provisional applications based on SSC qualifications, subject to candidates meeting HSC requirements after the supplementary results.

Comilla University will accept applications from December 10 to 31, including from retakers, and hold tests on February 5-7.

The 20-university General, Science and Technology cluster expects to accommodate supplementary passers, with admission tests planned for March. Shahjalal University of Science and Technology is considering similar arrangements.

Meanwhile, several universities have relaxed admission requirements, although lower GPA thresholds will not benefit candidates unable to apply before the deadlines.

JU reduced its combined SSC-HSC GPA requirement for mathematical and physical sciences from 8.5 to 7.5 and for biological sciences from 9.0 to 8.0.

The agricultural cluster lowered its threshold from 8.5 to 8.0, counting the fourth subject while requiring at least GPA 4.0 in each examination.

Kuet reduced the required combined HSC grade points in mathematics, physics, chemistry and English from 18 to 16. DU retained its overall thresholds but relaxed departmental requirements.

RU lowered the combined GPA requirement for humanities and business studies from 7.0 to 6.5.

JnU reduced the thresholds for science from 7.5 to 7.0, arts and law and social sciences from 6.5 to 6.0, and fine arts from 6.0 to 5.5.

On November 14, Education Minister ANM Ehsanul Hoque Milon urged DU to extend its application deadline for candidates whose grades improve after re-scrutiny.

However, he said DU, Buet and medical colleges need not delay admission tests for supplementary examinees, citing 15 lakh higher education seats against six lakh HSC passers.

UGC figures put public university main-campus seats at 63,656.

At a November 11 briefing, Campaign for Popular Education (CAMPE) Executive Director Rasheda K Choudhury urged universities to reconsider their decisions.

CAMPE also called for a supplementary examination policy and presented a letter addressed to the prime minister for dispatch.

Speaking to The Daily Star yesterday, Rasheda said universities could cut holidays or hold classes during Ramadan to adjust schedules without excluding retakers. 

She called for clear policy guidelines, announced in advance, to avoid similar problems in future admission sessions.

Prof Mohammad Mojibur Rahman of DU’s Institute of Education and Research called for coordination among the government, UGC and universities. 

He proposed at least two admission intakes a year and said supplementary exams should maintain regular HSC standards and called for a comprehensive education policy. 

UGC Chairman Prof Mamun Ahmed could not be reached for comment despite repeated phone calls.
